meta.what_it_is: A STRENGTH ranking -- who would win a match -- that moves with every result. Not a resume ranking and not what the committee does (R3).
meta.season_z_scale: observed net pts/set divided by the between-team SD (2.44), NOT z-scored against whoever happens to have played -- that would score the best of six teams as if it were the best of 348
meta.k_source: measured: forecast_blend_k_2025.json (k=10 beats derived, CI clear of zero)

k_measured_vs_derived.decision: keep the derived value -- the difference is not distinguishable from zero, and the derivation tracks the data while a pasted constant does not

meta.k_note: matches at which this season and the preseason weigh equally; k = per-match variance / the PROJECTION'S OWN error variance, not the between-team variance -- the projection is far better than an average team and is weighted accordingly
meta.caveat_schedule: the opponent IS adjusted for from match one: a result is scored as the strength it implies (opponent's rating + margin, home court removed). What is still thin early is the opponent's own rating, which is the preseason projection until a schedule graph exists
meta.score_scale_note: mean and SD across ALL 348 teams, not just the ones shown -- a scale computed from the top 25 would measure the spread among the best
